title: Library
summary: The library lists every track the station can play: songs, jingles, news, and segments. Here you describe tracks, put them into playlists, listen to them before they go to air, and check and fix their sound quality.

entities.text: One audio file with its title, artist, length, and type. The file stays on disk in the media folder; the library only stores where it is.
Where the file is, relative to the media folder, with forward slashes, for example music/summer-song.mp3.
A label such as music, jingle, news, or segment. It helps you filter and find tracks. It does not change how the track is chosen.
The result of the audio analysis: format, sample rate, channels, loudness, and peak compared with the broadcast standard in the settings.

Fix loudness brings the loudness to the station level and keeps the format. Optimize track also converts the file to the broadcast standard. A button appears only when it removes at least one issue. Choose whether the fixed file replaces the original or is kept as an optimal copy next to it.

Delete (N) next to Clear selection removes up to 1,000 selected tracks from the library in one step. The files stay on disk. A track that has aired, is planned, or is a timed insert of a clock or a one-time insert is kept: the result lists each kept track with the reason, links the clocks that use it, and leaves it selected.

Listeners see the library title and artist, not the tags inside the file: Icecast shows "Artist - Title", and a jingle without an artist shows its title alone. Correct one title by clicking it in the list, or select tracks and use Rename (N) to find and replace text in all their titles, for example to remove "[www.site.com]". Preview shows the new titles first; Apply writes them. The text is found literally, not as a pattern. A new title is heard on air for items queued after the change; items already queued keep the old title.

Reviewed marks a track you have checked: title, artist, quality, bitrate, and loudness. After an import, filter Reviewed: Not reviewed, check the tracks, and select them for Mark reviewed (N), or use the Reviewed switch on a track's page. Any change of a track's content clears the mark, so the track comes back into Not reviewed: a new title, artist, or file, and a Fix loudness or Optimize that changes the file. Playlists, type, notes, and play rules do not clear it.

The list shows one page at a time; choose the rows per page and move with the arrows under the table, which also show how many tracks match. Click a column header to sort the whole library, or the whole filtered list, by that column; click again to reverse the order. Tracks without the value, such as no artist or no length, are always last. The page and the order are kept when you open a track and come back.
Plays the track in your browser only. A preview never goes to air and does not count as a play.
The performer of a track, kept on the Artists page. The artist interval of play rules counts plays per artist, so each artist has one entry with a unique name. Jingles and station IDs need no artist.

Cut the edges of a track without changing the file: applause at the end, talk or noise at the start. In Start and stop on the track page, drag the start and stop handles on the waveform or type the times, choose the fades (0 is a hard cut), and listen with Play from start point and Play last 5 s before stop. Save start and stop applies them: on air the track starts at the start point and ends at the stop point, and the plan fits it by that shorter length. A cut leaves at least 5 seconds on air. Reset goes back to the whole file. While the track is on air or queued the points cannot be saved; save after it has played. When the track is planned, the planned hours that hold it are rebuilt with the new cut.

Click the waveform to place the cursor. Space plays or pauses the file from the cursor, I sets the start point and O the stop point at the cursor, + and − zoom, and 0 shows the whole track; Ctrl with the mouse wheel zooms around the pointer. A quiet track is enlarged so its loudest point fills the height; the toolbar shows by how much (for example ×2.6), and Real level draws it as loud as it is. The scale on the left of the waveform marks the real level in dB, from the loudest point at the top and bottom edges to −∞ at the centre. On a start or stop handle, ← and → move it by 100 ms, with Shift by 1 s, with Alt by 10 ms; Page Up and Page Down by 10 s; Home and End move it as far as it can go.

The In plan column shows the next planned start of a track, a mark next to the title shows that it is on air or queued, and the Playlists column counts its playlists (hover for their names). Filter In plan: Yes or No, or tick Without playlist to find tracks nothing uses. The Length column shows the length on air; a cut track shows a mark, and its tooltip gives the length of the file.

usage: Search by title or artist, or filter by playlist, type, quality, or reviewed. Open a track with Edit on its row to edit its details, its playlists, and its play rules, and to see what the analysis measured. Select tracks with the checkboxes to analyse them again, fix them, rename them, mark them reviewed, or delete them; the selection is kept when you change the page or the sort, so you can select tracks on several pages. The checkbox in the header selects the tracks on the current page. A new search or filter clears the selection. Use the play button on any row to check what a track sounds like.
steps: Bring new files in through the Import page, or copy a file into the media folder and click Add track.
For a track added by hand, enter the title, the artist, the type, and the file path.
Choose the playlists the track belongs to.
Add play rules if the track may only play at certain times (mostly jingles).
Filter by quality Issues, select the tracks, and use Fix loudness or Optimize track where offered.
After an import, filter Not reviewed, correct the titles, and mark the checked tracks reviewed.
Press play to check the result.
mistakes: Entering a full path such as C:\media\song.mp3 or /media/song.mp3. Enter only the part inside the media folder.
Forgetting the duration of a track whose file cannot be read: a track without a duration is never planned.
Expecting the type to control rotation. Only playlists, clocks, and rules decide when a track plays.
Choosing Replace the original when you may want the original back. Replace deletes it; an optimal copy keeps it on disk.
Expecting a fix for a low bitrate. Detail lost in the source cannot be restored; replace the file with a better one.
Expecting Delete to free disk space. It removes tracks from the library only; the files stay in the media folder.
Marking a track reviewed and then changing its title or optimizing it. The change clears the mark; mark it again after the change.
Expecting a cut to change the file. Start and stop points only tell the air where to begin and end; the file stays whole, and Reset brings it back.

example.title: Adding a morning jingle
example.text: The file jingles/good-morning.mp3 is in the media folder. Add a track titled "Good morning", type jingle, file path jingles/good-morning.mp3, playlist "Jingles", and the play rule "Morning 06:00 to 10:00". Press play to check it, then save. The jingle now fills jingle slots only in the morning.

operations.create: The file must already be in the media folder. The panel does not upload files; use the Import page for new files.
operations.edit: Changing the playlists or rules affects only hours that are not planned yet or are rebuilt.
operations.delete: A track that has aired or is planned cannot be deleted, so the played-tracks list stays complete; a track used as an insert cannot be deleted until it is removed from the clock or the planned hour. Remove such a track from its playlists instead. Deleting selected tracks applies the same rules to each track: the others are deleted, and the kept ones stay selected with the reason.

title.label: Title
title.text: The name shown in lists and in the stream metadata: listeners see this title and the artist, not the tags of the file. A change applies to items queued after saving. Line breaks and tabs are not allowed; extra spaces are removed.

artist_id.label: Artist
artist_id.text: Leave empty for material without an artist, such as jingles. The artist interval of play rules uses this field.

type_id.label: Type
type_id.text: A label for filtering and badges. It does not limit which clocks can use the track.

file_path.label: File path
file_path.text: Relative to the media folder, with forward slashes, for example music/song.mp3. No drive letters and no "..".

duration_ms.label: Duration
duration_ms.text: Length of the track in milliseconds. Read from the file when possible. A track without a duration is not planned.

playlist_ids.label: Playlists
playlist_ids.text: Every playlist the track belongs to. A track can be in several playlists.

rule_ids.label: Play rules
rule_ids.text: Rules of this track only. The rules of its playlists apply as well, and all must pass.

quality_ok.label: Quality OK
quality_ok.text: Your own decision that the track is good enough, or not. It overrides the analysis result until the next analysis.

reviewed.label: Reviewed
reviewed.text: Your mark that you have checked the track. It is saved at once, not with Save. A change of the title, artist, or file clears it, so save such changes first.

quality_notes.label: Quality notes
quality_notes.text: Your own notes about the file, for example "quiet intro".

force.label: Decode again
force.text: Off: a file that has not changed is only checked again against the current settings, which is quick. On: every file is decoded and measured again.

output.label: Fixed file
output.text: Optimal copy: the fixed file is written next to the original as name.optimal.ext and the track plays it; the original stays on disk. Replace: the fixed file takes the original's place and the original is deleted.

cue_in_ms.label: Start
cue_in_ms.text: Where the track starts on air, from the start of the file, as m:ss.mmm. 0:00.000 is the start of the file. Moving it from the start proposes the station's default fade in.

cue_out_ms.label: Stop
cue_out_ms.text: Where the track ends on air, as m:ss.mmm. The length of the file is its end. It must be after the start and leave at least 5 seconds on air. Moving it from the end proposes the station's default fade out.

fade_in_ms.label: Fade in
fade_in_ms.text: How long the sound rises from silence after the start point, 0 to 5000 ms. 0 is a hard cut.

fade_out_ms.label: Fade out
fade_out_ms.text: How long the sound falls to silence before the stop point, 0 to 5000 ms. 0 is a hard cut. The fades together must fit between the points.
